cases.why: a listed game is never given the cancelled state, so it reads 'started' on the Week Board for the rest of the season, #280's finding.
a listed game that was played after all is still called cancelled, so a real final score is hidden and the game reads as not graded.
a cancelled game still counts as unfinished, so its week is read by every weekend refresh, TV read and team-news read for the rest of the season.
a cancellation counts against every week, so one cancelled game closes a week whose own last game is still to be graded.
cases.find: return sum(1 for s, w, _, _ in cancelled if (s, w) == (season, week))

cases.why: an entry with no link is accepted, so a game can be taken out of every count on an unsourced word.
the warning fires as soon as a game has no score after kickoff, so every Monday-morning refresh nags about Sunday night's game while its feed catches up.
the card has no line for the cancelled state, so a cancelled game's card says nothing at all about why it was never graded.
cases.find: if(g.status === 'cancelled') return 'Cancelled · not played, so not graded';
